title: Okse-Filet (Beef Fillet)
description: Prepared with beef, fat, and gravy or stock.

ingredients.name: 1½ kg beef fillet (calculated as ¼ kg per person)
Tomato purée or Maggi bouillon cubes, if needed
French bread or household bread for the base

steps: Remove the sinews and fat from the fillet before larding it.
Lard the fillet thickly in neat rows with fine, fresh speck strips.
Brown the fillet in butter on a roasting pan or on the stovetop, without piercing it as this causes it to lose juice.
When brown on both sides, place it in a roasting pan in a hot oven, pour some gravy over it, and roast with frequent basting for half an hour.
When the fillet is roasted, strain off the gravy and make a strong, smooth gravy sauce as for roast beef.
If the gravy is not strong enough, improve it with tomato purée or Maggi bouillon cubes.
For presentation, take a slice of French bread or household bread, cut off the upper crust, and attach it to the center of an elongated platter with a mixture of flour and egg white.
On this base, arrange the roasted fillet, sliced thinly and overlapped together.
Surround the base with vegetables and arrange herb salads in shells or bird's nests around the presentation.

title: Oksekødfars (Beef Forcemeat)
description: Prepared with beef, fat or pork, and onion.

ingredients.name: 125 g tallow or fresh fat pork

steps: Cut the meat and if you do not have a meat grinder, pound it with a meat hammer to remove sinews more easily.

Work in 3 tablespoons flour, 2 to 3 eggs, salt, pepper and 1 small grated onion.

Add milk very gradually, stirring constantly in the same direction, as the forcemeat will easily separate otherwise. For this portion use 1/4 to 1 liter milk, but this depends on how long the forcemeat is being worked.
If you have a meat grinder, it is much easier to prepare the forcemeat.

title: Oksesteg (Roast Beef)
description: Prepared with beef or steak or tenderloin, salt, and water.

ingredients.name: Beef (Thick steak, tenderloin, or thin steak)

steps: When purchasing, allow 1/4 kilogram (1/2 pound) per person.
Beat the meat well with a meat mallet before rinsing.
Place it in the roasting pan and put it in the hot oven for a few minutes before pouring boiling water with some salt into the pan.
This way the pores contract, and the meat becomes juicier.
When placing the meat in the pan, turn the tenderloin upward, i.e., with the outer fillet (the most meaty side) down toward the pan.
It must be basted frequently during roasting, which must proceed very evenly.
A beef roast (thick steak) of 5 to 6 kilograms (10 to 12 pounds) needs 3 hours of roasting and is still juicy and red in the meat without being bloody.
Half an hour before serving, skim most of the gravy from the meat, and remove the fat, while pouring a little more water onto the pan to prevent the meat from browning too much.

title: Oksesteg (Roast Beef)
description: Prepared with beef, beer, and salt.

ingredients.name: A piece of beef (thick roast) of 5 to 6 kg

steps: Pour boiling water with salt into the oven pan before placing the meat.
Place the roast in the pan with the outer fillet side facing down towards the pan.
Roast for 3 hours, basting frequently and evenly.
Half an hour before serving, remove most of the gravy from the roast and skim off the fat, then pour a little water back into the pan to prevent the roast from burning while it remains in the oven.
For the sauce, brown butter and bake flour in it, then thin with the gravy to make a fairly thin sauce. Let it boil for about 10 minutes before serving.
The sauce should have a nice brown color.
Arrange the roast on a hot platter with the tender side facing up, as it lay in the oven.
Serve with boiled potatoes, peas, cucumbers, pickles, preserves, or compote.
Optionally, rub the roast with garlic or place a couple of onions on the pan to roast together, and roast some fresh or salted tomatoes with the roast.

steps: Mix 1 pot of sour cream into 5 pots of milk in an enameled pot, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and place in a lukewarm oven so the milk becomes warm (15 degrees), but not hot, as it would then become grainy.

Then remove the lid, place a thin, clean linen cloth, dipped in cold water and wrung out, over a colander.
Place the curdled milk in the cloth and leave for 5 to 6 hours so the whey can drain completely.
Shortly before serving, turn the milk from the cloth onto a dish and serve with whipped cream on top, and sweet cream and powdered sugar on the side.

Alternatively, reduce the amount of sour cream and take a corresponding amount of buttermilk instead. The faster the milk curdles, the better. For this reason, 4 drops of rennet (obtained from the apothecary) can be added; the milk is warmed to 15 degrees, left to stand, and treated as previously mentioned.

title: Oxekjodsuppe (Beef Broth)
description: A soup made with beef, carrot, and onion.
steps: Rinse the meat in several changes of water, but do not let it soak. Place the meat in cold water with a carrot, onion, and a little salt over the fire. Skim when the broth first comes to a boil. Make a bouquet of celery leaves, leeks, and parsley. When the fat has been removed from the broth, which happens about an hour before the meat is tender, add the bouquet along with carrots, celery, and parsley roots that have been scraped and washed but not cut into pieces. The roots should be cooked in the broth at the same time as the meat; both should become tender at approximately the same time. Remove both the meat and roots, clean the roots, cut them into pieces, and place them in the serving dish to receive the broth. Remove the bouquet before it falls apart. Use slow cooking with steady, even heat for the best broth; wood fire cannot be used well. The lid must close well and should only be removed when the broth needs skimming. Add water for thinning only with boiling water if necessary. When everything is removed, strain the broth through a fine sieve. Let it stand briefly to settle, remove the fat, and pour it back into the pot carefully so the sediment does not come along. When the broth comes to a boil again, it will throw off a little more scum, and this should also be removed if you want it perfectly clear. After this, add the dumplings, though it is best to cook these in water or thin broth separately, as the broth becomes less clear and diminishes somewhat by cooking them in it. When serving the broth, you can add a piece of white sugar, which gives it a pleasant flavor. This portion will require approximately 2-3 hours of cooking.

title: Oxesteg (Beef Roast)
description: Prepared with beef, salt, and butter.

ingredients.name: Beef, preferably from a young, well-fed animal
Butter, the best quality fresh butter
Bouillon, ale, or water (optional, used sparingly)

steps: Select a piece of meat from a young, well-fed animal, recognizable by its beautiful red color (not dark red), fine fat threads throughout, and white and clear bone. Prefer the tenderloin, though the thick roast, brisket, or leg and neck can also be used if the animal was young and fat.
Allow the meat to hang for several days, according to the season, before roasting.
Calculate about half a pound of roast per person, preferring a larger piece to a smaller one.
Heat the oven appropriately according to the size of the piece to be roasted, so that the pores in the meat contract and it retains its juices.
Scatter salt in the pan to prevent the roast from sticking.
Place the roast in the pan with the best side up, which should also be uppermost when serving. Never turn the roast during roasting.
If the meat is very fatty, it will soon melt enough fat to provide sufficient liquid; otherwise, add a little butter to the pan.

Only if there is danger that the butter or fat will become too brown, pour a little bouillon, ale, or water under the roast, but only sparingly, as much liquid produces a poor roast that seems boiled.
After the roast has been in the oven for half an hour, drip it with the sauce from the pan, or pour new butter over it.
Continue to drip the roast from time to time, but do not keep the oven door open too long.
If the roast threatens to become too brown, place a piece of buttered butcher's paper over it, lifting it each time the roast is to be dripped.
Roast mainly at brisk heat in the beginning; towards the end, the heat may be reduced somewhat.

When done, the roast should be red inside but not bloody, and the juice should flow out when cut. A 12-pound roast requires approximately 2½ hours, and one generally allows a quarter hour more for each additional 2 pounds.
When the roast is removed from the oven and placed on the serving dish, pour all the juice that has run into the pan into a pot along with the scrapings from the pan.
Boil it with thin soup or gravy and water, strain it, skim the fat, brown butter very lightly, stir a little flour into it, thin it with the roasting gravy, and give it all a quick boil.
Serve the roast with this sauce, along with raw-peeled, boiled, or browned potatoes, and according to the season with salad, cucumbers, aspics, etc.
Provide very hot plates for this and all roasts.

title: Pears (Perer)
description: Prepared with pears, white sugar, and lemon peel or ginger or pears.

Lemon juice (if pears are very sweet)

steps: If unripe, put the pears in boiling water and cook slightly until they begin to soften

The next day cover with paper dipped in brandy and seal

title: Pears Cooked in a Pot (Perer kogte i Krukke)
description: Prepared with pears, white sugar, and brandy.

ingredients.name: 1 pound crushed white sugar per pound of pears

steps: Peel the pears, remove the blossom and trim the stem

Weigh the pears
Layer them in a pot with 1 pound crushed white sugar per pound of fruit
Pour nearly 3 pints of brandy over
Place a cover or lid that fits well at the sides over the pot
Seal around the edge with rye flour and water made into a thick dough so no steam can escape
Place the pot in an oven that is not as hot as needed for roasting
Leave until juice begins to come out, then remove the pot and check if the seal has loosened and put it back
Repeat for 1 day until the pears are done
Keep the pot sealed until needed; later tie it well, if possible with a bladder, so the brandy does not lose its strength
Peaches may be preserved the same way, as well as raspberries and strawberries

title: Plukfisk (Flaked Fish)
description: Prepared with fish, malt, and nutmeg or pepper.
steps: Plukfisk is usually made when you have leftover fish from the day before.
Pick the meat from the bones.

Melt a good piece of butter, stir in flour; gradually stir in malt until it has a suitable thickness, then add the fish and ground nutmeg or pepper, cook a little, finally add a small piece of sugar and salt.
Before the salt is added, you can bind the fish with an egg yolk, which gives it a good flavor.
Then place slices of French bread, which have first been baked in butter on a plate, and pour the fish over.
You can also place the warm plukfisk in a deep plate, sprinkle a layer of ground bread a finger's thickness over it, pour melted butter over it and place it in the oven where it is baked light brown.
To prevent the bread from sinking into the fish, it must be fairly thick and is therefore best made by binding it with two egg yolks.
You can of course also use freshly cooked fish. Cooked salt cod can also be used, but it must be chopped fine and requires much butter.
If you do not want to use bread for the salt fish, small diced carrots and pepper can be added.

description: A pudding made with beef, raisins, and currants.

ingredients.name: 125 grams beef bone marrow, cut into smaller pieces
1 teaspoonful soda, dissolved in 1.25 deciliters milk

steps: Into 0.5 kilogram of flour, stir 0.25 kilogram of chopped beef kidney fat, 125 grams of beef bone marrow cut into smaller pieces, 0.25 kilogram of raisins, 125 grams of currants, both plucked and scalded, 125 grams of finely cut citron peel, 0.25 kilogram of powdered or caster sugar, 1.25 deciliters of rum, 4 eggs, and 1 teaspoonful of soda dissolved in 1.25 deciliters of milk.
The batter can be placed in a cloth that is buttered in the middle and sprinkled with flour.
The cloth is then gathered and tied with a ribbon.
It is cooked in the cloth in a pot with plenty of water for about 3 hours.
Plum pudding can, like any other pudding, be cooked in a buttered and floured mold.
At serving, a hole is cut in the top; into it are placed some pieces of sugar, which are covered with rum, just as the sides of the pudding are covered.
It is lit and must be brought to the table burning.
Serve with fruit sauce.

title: Plumbudding (Plum Pudding)
description: A pudding made with rum, kidney, and beef marrow.
steps: Remove the crusts from 8 French breads.
Cut the breads into slices, dip them in rum, then soak in sweet milk until soaked through.

Beat 14 whole eggs with 13 pægle sweet cream and 1 pægle good rum and add to the mixture, beating well together.
Pour the entire mixture into a sugar-glazed mold.
Place in boiling water and cook for approximately 4 hours.
Turn out onto a serving platter.
Pour 1 pægle warm rum over it and set it alight, so the pudding is served flaming.

title: Pomeransskal (Candied Orange Peel)
description: Prepared with orange peel and sugar.
steps: If a large number of lemons or oranges are used in the household, the peels can be preserved and used in baking where candied orange peel or other citrus peel is otherwise used.
Remove the peels in 2 halves and soak in cold water for 3 to 4 days, changing the water daily.
Cook the peels tender in water under a lid, then remove and place on a strainer.
Pour the sugar over the peels.
After 3 to 4 days, pour off the syrup and cook until very smooth, then pour back over the peels.
3 days later, pour everything into the pot and boil for 5 to 6 minutes.
Remove the peels and place in a jar, then bring the syrup to a boil before pouring over. Seal.

Place the meat in the sauce and set to cool.

title: Postej med Høns og Tomat-Sauce (Pâté with Chicken and Tomato Sauce)
description: A sauce made with tomato, fish, and chickens.

ingredients.name: 1/2 kg (1 pound) scraped fish for farce

steps: The pâté must be baked in a mold, either porcelain or a common metal form with a firm base.
For a metal mold, use short pastry for lining, as the pâté would otherwise be exposed to too strong heat.
Make the short pastry from 1/2 kg (1 pound) flour (see Nr. 21) and roll it out fairly thin.
Line the buttered mold with the pastry; it must be ample enough to hang 2 to 3 centimeters (1 inch) over the edge of the mold.
Lay a layer of fish farce (see Nr. 205), approximately 2 to 3 centimeters (1 inch) thick, over the short pastry on both the bottom and sides.
Boil 3 chickens until tender and remove the meat from the bones, placing it in the center of the mold.
Make a sauce from butter and flour, thinned with the chicken stock, add tomato purée to taste and Madeira or Sherry.
Pour enough sauce into the mold to roughly cover the meat.
Place a layer of farce on top and finally a layer of short pastry.
Fold the pastry hanging over the mold up onto the lid so it closes well.
Brush the lid with egg and bake the pâté for about one hour in a well-heated oven.
At serving, place the mold on a dish on which a folded napkin has been laid.
Conceal the mold either by fastening a napkin around it or using an embroidered band.
Prepare the sauce for the pâté at the same time you make the interior sauce to pour over the meat; thin it and add more tomato purée, Maggi's bouillon cubes, and wine if needed.
Small fish balls may be added to the sauce boat.
Champignons may be used instead of tomatoes.

Bind the jar when they are cold

title: Presse-Sylte (Pressed Pork Aspic)
description: Prepared with pork, pork or tenderloin, and bay leaves.

ingredients.name: 1/2 to 1 kg (1 to 2 pounds) lean pork shoulder or tenderloin

steps: Split the pork head and clean it; remove the brains, eyes, and tongue
Clean the ears carefully or cut them off entirely if preferred
Cut away the snout cartilage to better drain the blood, and clean the snout
Soak the head in water overnight, then rinse it several times in cold water
Scald it in boiling water and it is then ready for cooking
Place it over the fire in cold water with salt and whole pepper; skim the broth well when it boils
Cook 1/2 to 1 kg of lean pork shoulder or tenderloin together with the head; this will be distributed in the aspic
When the head is cooked so much that the meat loosens from the bones, remove it
Spread a cloth wrung out in boiling water in a mold or deep dish
Cut the rind from the head and use it to line the mold
Cut the remaining meat into smaller pieces, distribute the fat and lean meat, and sprinkle salt and ground pepper between layers
Bind the cloth tightly together with a band and place a lid with weight on top; the lid should not be larger than to fit down into the mold, as the aspic shrinks greatly during pressing
The next day, remove the cloth and place the aspic in a cold, mild brine made of 2 handfuls salt, some bay leaves, whole pepper and a little vinegar, and pour 2 L (2 pots) of boiling water over it
When serving, cut the aspic into slices and eat with vinegar, pepper, mustard and beets
The tongue can be boiled and added to the aspic, or else salted as a condiment
The head broth can be used for pea soup, kale soup, or brown cabbage soup, or boiled together with herbs and marrow bones and used in the household as economy broth

description: A pudding made with sour cream, egg yolks, and almonds.
steps: Whip the cream slightly and bring to a boil with the sugar.
Melt the butter without clarifying it; when it begins to boil, brown 6 ounces of flour in it.
Gradually add the boiling cream to this mixture.
When almost cold, add 20 egg yolks which have been whipped slightly, cardamom, lemon peel, and a little chopped almonds.
Beat the 20 egg whites stiff and fold them in just before pouring into the form.
Boil for about 2 hours; serves 20 persons.
It can be made in half size. Serve with red sauce.
16 eggs can be used, but then it serves only 16 persons.

description: A cake made with egg yolks, powdered sugar, and juice.
steps: Beat 20 egg yolks for 3 quarter-hours with 1 pound powdered sugar.

Stir vanilla essence into the finished compote.

title: Rabarbersaft (Rhubarb Syrup)
description: Prepared with rhubarb, powdered sugar, and water.

ingredients.name: 125 gr (1/4 lb) powdered sugar per 1 liter (1 pot) juice

steps: This syrup is quite excellent and also the cheapest available. Since the stalks contain much acidity, they can be boiled 3 times, and yet the third batch of syrup is good and long-lasting. At the end of May or beginning of June is when the stalks are most juicy.

First Boiling: Cut 50 good thick stalks into 8 centimeter (1/2 quarter) long pieces and rinse well. Cover the bottom of the preserving pot with 1/2 liter (1/2 pot) of boiling water to prevent the stalks from burning. Boil them completely under regular stirring and over very low heat. Pour the mass into a stretched jelly cloth until the juice has partially run off after 1/2 hour.

Second Boiling: Put the rhubarb mass back in the pot together with 2 liters (2 pots) of boiling water and boil for 10 minutes, then strain in the cloth again until the juice has almost completely run off.
Third Boiling: This time add 1.5 liters (1.5 pots) of boiling water, and boil the mass again for 10 minutes before straining in the cloth, so that the last bit of juice can run off.

Now you can, if you wish, mix all 3 batches of juice and boil them together, but the first drained juice is decidedly the strongest and should be preserved separately. Only 125 gr (1/4 lb) sugar is added to each liter (pot) of juice, which is boiled and skimmed for 10 minutes.
Dissolve 2 small teaspoons of salicylic acid in some of the warm juice and distribute throughout the entire batch.
The salicylic acid must not be omitted. Pour the juice hot into bottles which are tied immediately with parchment paper.

Rhubarb syrup is a refreshing summer drink and can be made as a good dessert at little expense. Even after the stalks have been boiled 3 times, water can be added again and they can boil for 10 minutes before straining in the cloth and hanging until the next day. The juice that runs through can be made into rhubarb pudding and if necessary mixed with a few drops of red fruit coloring.
From ordinary good large stalks, about 14 bottles of good syrup can be obtained from this amount.

title: Ribsvin (Currant Wine)
description: Prepared with currants, powdered sugar, and water.

ingredients.name: Alternatively, 4 pounds of the currants may be replaced with 4 pounds red raspberries

steps: Place the sugar in a clean bucket
The currants, which are not stripped from their stems, are wrung out in a clean linen cloth and the juice is poured over the sugar, stirred well, and left until the next day
Pour 13½ pails water over the wrung-out berries, which likewise stands until the next day, then strain through a sieve and press well
Pour the juice into the barrel along with the water from the wrung-out berries, and if this is not sufficient to fill the barrel, fill it with water
To make room for the juice to ferment, draw off 2 bottles of juice from the barrel and set aside loosely corked
Shake the barrel vigorously to promote mixing and place it in a cellar or other cool place
Seal it only loosely and leave it thus for 6 weeks to ferment
When fermentation has taken place, add the 2 bottles of juice previously removed, which have also fermented, then seal the barrel well and seal with clay
It then rests completely until around February, when the wine can be drawn off and corked well

To serve warm, heat the wine over the fire with 1 crushed cardamom per pail, a little whole cinnamon, a couple of cloves and sugar to taste; when the wine is about to boil, light it briefly and then remove from the fire

ingredients.name: Cooked vegetables such as Brussels sprouts, peas, or asparagus

steps: Cook the rice as described in recipe 502, but omit the raisins
Wet small molds lightly and line them with the rice mixture
In the center, place cooked finely chopped vegetables such as Brussels sprouts, peas, or asparagus, or any cooked vegetables that suit soup
Add finely chopped parsley or chervil
Cover with another layer of cooked rice
Turn these small puddings out onto a warm platter while still warm
Serve with the soup, allowing one rice puff per person
Small timbale molds can be used

title: Roasted Pork Shoulder (Stegt Svinekam)
description: Prepared with pork, coloring, and salt.

ingredients.name: 2½ kg (5 lbs) pork shoulder, with all fat trimmed

steps: Wash the pork shoulder in cold water, sprinkle with salt, and place on a roasting pan, which is set in a hot oven.
Add boiling water to the pan, and baste the shoulder well during roasting, which lasts 1½ to 2 hours, depending on its thickness.
If roasting in a pot, it must be browned first.
Strain the broth, and in some of the skimmed fat, cook the flour, which is thinned with the broth to a suitable smooth sauce, colored with food coloring.
Serve with vegetables and preserves as mentioned for roast pork belly.

title: Rod-Grod af Sago (Sago Jelly)
description: Prepared with sago, juice, and water.
steps: The best large sago grains are particularly suited for rod-grod, in which no starch is then needed.
If you get the best sago, which swells the most, you can reckon 1 pound grains to 4 to 5 quarts water.
Add juice and sugar to taste.
The grains should be cooked more in the water before juice and sugar are added, and thereafter the whole gets a good boil.
Spoon a spoonful onto a plate to see if it is sufficiently thick.
If it is too thick, it can be thinned with a little boiling water, but if it is too thin, there is nothing else to do but smooth it with a spoonful of corn-starch dissolved in cold water.
The best pearl sago can cook out to a clear jelly, and it becomes best with juice; but if preferred, it can also be made with red wine and lemon juice.

title: Rollmops (Herring Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with herring, onions, and peppercorns.
steps: Clean the fresh herring and remove the bone
These herring, which are cut in the belly, are spread out
Mix 6 coarsely chopped onions with 25 gr (5 quintal) whole peppercorns, 75 gr (15 quintal) sugar and 100 gr (20 quintal) salt and distribute this mixture on the herring
Roll the herring from the tail upward and bind them with bands or gather them with a sausage pin
Cook the herring in vinegar water in which 15 to 20 bay leaves are added
The herring remain in the broth they are cooked in and are also arranged in this
Serve cold
If using cured herring instead of fresh herring, economize on the salt that is placed inside the herring and cook them in as little liquid as possible

title: Rom-Budding (Rum Pudding)
description: A pudding made with rum, egg yolks, and icing sugar.

ingredients.name: cold fruit juice sauce, preferably of raspberry juice

steps: Stir 5 egg yolks with 125 Gr (1/4 S) icing sugar and whisk into 1/2 L (1/2 Pot) half-skimmed boiling milk
Cook to custard consistency
Dissolve 12 leaves of isinglass in 1 1/4 Dl (1/2 Pægl) boiling water and stir into the custard
When the custard has cooled, add 1/4 L (1 Pægl) white rum and cream foam from 1/4 L (1 Pægl) cream
When the mixture begins to set, pour it into a wetted mold

Melt a slice of butter on a pan and add the eggs.

title: Rombudding B (Rum Pudding B)
description: A pudding made with rum, egg yolks, and cream.

ingredients.name: 10 quintals isinglass dissolved in boiling water

steps: Stir 4 egg yolks well with 4 tablespoons finely ground melis sugar.
Add 1 pail rum.
Whip 1 pot cream to thick foam and stir it into the egg yolks.
Finally add 10 quintals isinglass that has been cooled after dissolving in 1 pail boiling water.
Pour the mixture into a glass bowl and set to cool, and half an hour later the pudding is stiff and can be arranged.

title: Roræg (Scrambled Eggs)
description: Prepared with eggs, cream or milk, and butter.
steps: Beat 8 eggs well, first alone, then with 8 small spoonfuls of cream or good milk.
Put it in the pot or frying pan with an ounce of butter and a little salt.
It tastes good to add a little finely chopped parsley.
There must not be a high flame and do not stir, but scrape continually from the bottom with a spatula; if you stir round, the pieces will break apart and that is not the intention.
When you find them suitably stiff, take them off the fire.
They must not be too hard.
You can add cooked asparagus heads in them.
Count 3 eggs per person.

title: Roulettes of Roasted or Boiled Meat
description: Prepared with meat, onions, and bouillon.

Cook until smooth, then stir in 1 pound cooked, finely chopped meat, ground pepper and salt
When completely cold, take a little at a time and roll in ground bread, then in well-beaten eggs, then in bread again
Cook them in broth together with a little whole parsley to garnish
About 16 roulettes are made from this portion, using 5 rusks and 4 eggs
For a more piquant taste, 3 chopped anchovies can be sautéed with the onions, and a little white wine, a little lemon juice and nutmeg can be added to the mixture

title: Rug-Kiks, 1 (Rye Biscuits, 1)
description: A biscuit made with rye flour, cake, and caraway seeds.
steps: Place the rye flour and cake flour on a pastry board with the salt and caraway seeds
Take half of the cold margarine and chop it together with the flour using a knife until very finely crumbled
Work the vinegar and cold water into the dough with the knife
Gather the dough together with your hands and roll out with a rolling pin into a large sheet
Distribute the remaining margarine in small pieces over the dough
Fold the dough together and roll out 3-4 times as instructed for puff pastry (Nr. 22)
Let the dough rest in a cold place for a quarter of an hour
Roll out as thin as possible, dusted with flour without adding to the weight
Cut the biscuits into squares with a pastry cutter, prick with a fork, and place close together on a baking sheet
Bake light brown over good heat. Makes approximately 1 1/2 kilograms of excellent crispy biscuits that keep well for a long time, but should be placed briefly in a warm oven before serving

title: Rulleaal (Rolled Eel)
description: Prepared with eel, bay leaves, and vinegar.
steps: Skin the eel, cut off the head and tail, and clip off the fins with scissors
Cut the eel lengthwise along the back and remove the bone
Rinse it well and dry it in a fish cloth
Sprinkle it with salt, pepper and allspice and roll it tightly together from the tail
Bind it with yarn and sew it into a thin cloth
Place it over the fire in cold water with salt, whole pepper, bay leaves and vinegar
When cooked, remove it and place it in a press like rolled sausage
When the eel is cold, remove the bands, cut it into slices and place on a platter
Pour aspic (see recipe No. 247), made from the broth in which the eel was cooked, over it

title: Rullepølse (Rolled Sausage)
description: Prepared with beef or veal or lamb or meat, saltpeter, and onions.

ingredients.name: Beef, veal, or lamb meat, preferably from the best cuts
For veal sausages: fresh or salted, fatty bacon

steps: Lay the outer, fatty layer of beef on a board
Where the meat is thickest, cut some of it away and distribute it in the sausage along with any other smaller meat pieces
Sprinkle salt mixed with 1 teaspoon saltpeter, ground pepper, allspice, and 2 finely chopped onions
Roll the sausage very tightly
Insert a fork through the middle of the sausage to hold it together while sewing
Begin sewing from one end using a sewing needle and very strong thread, sewing as tightly as possible so it holds together after cooking
Bind the beef rolled sausage tightly with sailcloth before cooking
Beef rolled sausages require up to 2 hours of cooking; test tenderness by pricking with a fork
From one beef cut, 3 rolled sausages can be made
For veal rolled sausages, add fresh or salted fatty bacon and the same seasonings as mentioned
Lamb cuts are usually sufficiently fatty on their own; they can be prepared like beef and veal sausages or with chopped parsley, pepper, salt, and saltpeter
Beef rolled sausages are salted within 10 to 12 days, while veal and lamb rolled sausages require only 5 to 6 days
When the sausages are cooked, remove them from the boiling broth and place them in a press between 2 bacon boards with sufficient weight on top, and leave them until the next day

title: Rungsteds Lyksalighed (Rungsted's Happiness)
description: Prepared with egg whites, powdered sugar, and raspberry jam.
steps: Beat the 10 egg whites until very stiff.
Carefully stir in 10 tablespoons powdered sugar and 2 tablespoons raspberry jam without juice.
Pour onto flat baking sheets and dry in the oven like meringue. This must be done the day before.
On the day of serving, stir the 10 egg yolks (which have been covered) with 125 gr powdered sugar and add to 1/2 L boiling milk.
Make a good cream and add vanilla essence and 4 sheets isinglass dissolved in a small amount of water.
Stir the cream regularly until it is almost completely cold.
Pour over the egg whites and when set, top with whipped cream made from 1/2 L heavy cream.
Serve with macarons.

description: Prepared with cream, egg yolks, and powdered sugar.

Gently stir the mixture together so it appears striped
Pour into an ice bucket and put the lid on

description: Prepared with quince, powdered sugar, and water.

ingredients.name: 375 gr (0.75 lb) powdered sugar to 1/2 kg (1 lb) strained pulp

Cook the quinces until completely tender in water, remove and pass through the sieve.
Weigh the pulp and cook with the sugar until it is so firm that it does not immediately flow together after the spoon is drawn through it.
